{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693664985,"sessionID":"ses_e23ee75e4ffe9BOB4FdO6jc6ZC","part":{"id":"prt_1dc141066001VVTav1OZmDwSK2","messageID":"msg_1dc13efd30016CjQ6fHFQ3QkrK","sessionID":"ses_e23ee75e4ffe9BOB4FdO6jc6ZC","type":"text","text":"The shift is over. From minute 101 to the end, all four customer-facing services had 0% errors, with no throttles on and every service back at its normal replica count. Four faults were found and fixed; I didn't calculate the dollar cost of the shift.\n\n1. **events-queue lost its primary node (started at −25).** The errors set off a retry storm, and that took down mobile-api, partner-api and admin-portal. At minute 7 I throttled it, but the logs then showed \"primary node unreachable\", so the throttle alone was the wrong fix. I ran a failover at minute 25, but the retry load kept it overloaded. A short 70% throttle at minutes 45–49 cleared that.\n\n2. **Bad profile-svc deploy v75 (at −29) caused web-storefront's 4% error rate.** This was the costliest fault, at about $1,060 a minute. The deploy shrank the call deadline tenfold (`budget_ms / 10000`), so calls from reviews-svc timed out. I scaled profile-svc from 8 to 12 replicas first, in case the rollback triggered retries, then rolled it back at minute 47. It still went through a short retry overload, which cleared by itself. web-storefront was at 0% by minute 56, and I put profile-svc back to 8 replicas at minute 102.\n\n3. **Bad flags-svc deploy v118 (at −8).** It required TLS 1.3, so connections failed with \"TLS handshake failed\", and flags-svc went into a retry storm. I throttled it at 80% at minute 61, rolled it back at minute 70 and lifted the throttle at minute 77.\n\n4. **Config change cfg-35 on returns-svc (new at minute 68).** It changed `entry_ttl_s` from 600 to 1, which broke suggest-svc, recommendations-svc and flags-svc and took the three smaller services down again. I reverted it at minute 92 and throttled returns-svc for two minutes to clear the leftover retry overload.\n\nEvery mitigation went to a service that was actually at fault, so none should count as wasted. Most of the lost revenue came from web-storefront's 4% before the profile-svc rollback finished at about minute 53, and from the three smaller services being down for most of the first 100 minutes.","time":{"start":1794693664870,"end":1794693664978}}}
